records.failureSummary: Implemented and verified slice-1 of parseCsvLine in src/csv.mjs. The file is an ES module with a named export parseCsvLine(line): it returns [] immediately when typeof line !== "string" (no throw for null/undefined/number/boolean/object), and for string input returns line.split(","), preserving each field's leading/trailing whitespace with no trim and yielding empty-string fields for consecutive commas. It contains no quote parsing, escape handling, trim calls, loops, helpers, or new dependencies; only src/csv.mjs was modified (confirmed via git diff; the working tree change is exactly this function). Build (npm run build -> node --check src/csv.mjs) exits 0 and lint (npm run lint -> node --check src/csv.mjs) exits 0. node --test runs the 3 repo tests: 1 pass, 2 fail with 0 errors. The 2 failures are the FR-2 quoted-field test (parseCsvLine('a,\"b,c\",d') expected ['a','b,c','d'], got ['a','\"b','c\"','d']) and the FR-4 empty-line test (parseCsvLine('') expected [], got ['']); both exercise behavior explicitly excluded from this slice's task description and deferred to their later FR-2/FR-4 slices by the T2 design, so they are out of scope here. All FR-1/FR-6 acceptance criteria for this slice are met and pass.
